chapter: Louis Armstrong picture, Kid Rena record and Bunk
title: How the 1940 Kid Rena record session came about; Rene and his brother's signals
summary: A man came through Santiago to put together a jazz band. Rene says his brother would not record without him and describes their signals.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: How did they get that band together anyway to make that record?
Well, this fella came and got Santiago. He was the one. You know where the Santiago player get, though?

And he wanted to get some old music together, you see. And he wanted some jazz. So Santiago told him, saying, I wanted the most little jazzy fella we knowed around here. And he started around there, way around Budapetite time, you see. It was right there, you see. And my brother wouldn't play without me, you know. He didn't even want to play on a lot of other drums, you see. Because he knew what I was going to do. And you see, all he had to do was look at me and I knew what he wanted, you see. He would look at me, you see, and he'd throw me the sign what to do, you see. When he would throw me a sign, then I knew just what to do, you see. Then sometime I'd light up with a light risen like that, you see. Then he'd have his horn like that, grab it like that, and he'd do me this, you see. He was a little socket, you see. That's where I started pressing then, you see. And he's going to play that, you see. He's beginning to make all them high notes there, you see. That's why he wants plenty of support when he gets to them high notes. Because you see a man who's really up there, you know you can make a trumpet play at Boston's there. That's right. So then when he gave me that sign like that, I knew he was going up, you see. And he was going to play hard, you see. I didn't do nothing but just play straight, straight rhythm. But he didn't do nothing on the bracket. He told me, he had a funny idea though. He told me, he said, he's white, he had a funny idea too. He said, I ain't going to make them, that's what's going to catch my style. That's what was in his mind. And he just played that. He made me mad though. I was mad as I could be. Because I knew what he could do. But Jim never laid down, Jim cut on that. That's what made the band sound good too, if you want me to tell you. Jim, the tram won't play. Oh yeah. If I better play long that band, you'd avoid some hot stuff, see. I'd give him the rhythm, alright. I'd give him the rhythm, but he wasn't going to do it. Well the trouble is, why he made his mistake, he agreed to play for twenty-two hours and fifty cents a man. Instead of asking for a royalty on the record. That's what the other fellas, you know, they got mad and didn't want to play. We had the trouble, it's hard to get together. Well George Lewis, he was hard to get together, you know. He was alright. Well no, it wasn't George Lewis, it was P. Cooey, what else did I say? Lil Nelson. Well that fella never made that kind of money in an hour, you know. That sounds big to him, no?
